text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet asks Planning Ministry to draft long-term 2000-2025 national development plan.

- Jordan's Prime Minister Majali says reconciliation with Kuwait proceeding on right track. Ties between Kuwait and Amman were badly strained during 1990-91 Iraqi occupation over what Kuwait saw as Jordanian sympathy with Baghdad.
- Kuwait's state-run oil sector to provide 1,056 jobs for Kuwaiti graduates in 1997/98 fiscal year (July-June).
- Kuwait Stock Exchange's index rose 15.3 points to 2,439.7 on Sunday, continuing upward trend.
- Municipality to take immediate measures to check meat for bacteria.
- Officials representing Iraq, Kuwait and its 1991 Gulf War allies to meet on Kuwait-Iraq border to discuss fate of some 600 Kuwaitis missing since war.
- Kuwait Investment Co reports 11.5 percent rise in mid-year results to 5.2 million dinars ($17.1 million).
- Health Ministry denies ban on treatment of expatriates. A newspaper said last week the ministry had instructed specialised state-run hospitals to stop admitting foreign residents.
